name: Opening Drive v3
unit: eligible player and scheduled NFL week
evaluation_status: Historical development evaluation; these years were used in earlier research. Policies fixed before the v3 evaluation period; annual fits use earlier seasons only.
research_questions: Does a weekly conditional mean improve on v2 horizon points per scheduled game?
Does a correction to v2 improve on a direct weekly mean?
Does full history, a recent window, or recency weighting predict best?
Does personal scoring and residual history improve distribution forecasts beyond comparable-player pooling?
Does conditional scale or quantile boosting improve on pooled and shrunk personal residual distributions?
Are interval coverage, width, and tail probabilities useful across positions, workload, history length, and seasons?
Do regularized dependence estimates improve lineup distributions versus independent aggregation?
What evidence supports K/DST uncertainty, and how does mixed scoring differ from official league scoring?

controls.future_eligibility: Never use future appearances to choose candidate players
controls.features: Only completed earlier weeks; current-week outcomes never enter predictors
controls.historical_v2: Frozen chronological v2 forecasts when available; earlier fallback explicitly identified
controls.variance_targets: Earlier out-of-time errors; in-sample residuals cannot supply evaluation calibration
controls.selection: Separate mean and distribution selection from evaluation
controls.missing: Missing observations remain distinct from verified zero outcomes
controls.scoring: Preserve v2 offensive scoring; identify ESPN K/DST and official league scoring gaps
controls.original_artifacts: Preserve original model bytes and forecasts; publish v3 separately
controls.current_forecast: Reconstructed 2026 cutoffs from later captures, with publication time retained
